participant_materials.setup_placeholder: Study information and consent text will be supplied by the owner after the applicable ethics and recruitment process. This materials draft does not provide or imply ethics approval.
participant_materials.legend: Use all five facts together. The inputs are: whether the READ relation is supported at the named tier; whether a matched comparison was run and what its estimate, interval, and registered margin show; how the unsteered comparator was constructed; whether the registered coherence check passed; and the exact model, method, task, and tier scope. Apply them in this order: a tier change needs new tier-specific evidence; unsupported READ stays unresolved; supported READ with an untested comparison is diagnostic only; a missing comparison result or an interval crossing zero stays unresolved; a resolved result showing no superiority, or a wholly positive interval whose estimate is below the margin, is withheld; when the interval lower bound is above zero and the estimate meets or equals the margin, the result is withheld if coherence fails and is supported only if coherence passes. Display order carries no meaning.
participant_materials.tutorial: First answer which interface state follows from all five facts and the routing order in the legend. After you submit Q1, it is locked and Q2 appears. Q2 separately asks what evidence, baseline relation, scope boundary, or tier-specific evaluation is established or still needed. A formal trial counts as correct only when both answers are correct. Formal trials give no feedback. The Contract and Flat versions use the same facts, questions, options, and routing rule.

participant_materials.debrief: These were simulated teaching records with fabricated values. They assess structured rule application, not deep integration or real-world benefit. No item reports a current paper pass, and no response changes the paper's claims.

tokenization.algorithm: NFKC lowercase; tokens are maximal Unicode alphanumeric sequences; punctuation and symbols are separators.

heuristics.equal_length: Choose the option with token count closest to the median option-token count; ties use alphabetical key order.
heuristics.negation_marker: Choose the first option containing one of: neither, no, not, unknown, unavailable; otherwise A.
heuristics.modal_marker: Choose the first option containing one of: required, require, requires, now, must; otherwise A.
heuristics.read_lexical: Choose the first option containing the token READ; otherwise A.
heuristics.oracle_template: For each template choose its most frequent key across all items; ties use alphabetical key order.
heuristics.loo_template: For each held-out item choose the most frequent key among other uses of that template; ties use alphabetical key order.
heuristics.global_position: Choose the globally most frequent key; ties use alphabetical key order.
heuristics.single_row_q1: untested->Q1_DIAGNOSTIC; ci_high<=0->Q1_WITHHELD; ci_low<=0<=ci_high->Q1_UNRESOLVED; ci_low>0 and estimate>=margin->Q1_SUPPORTED; ci_low>0 and estimate<margin->Q1_WITHHELD; otherwise Q1_UNRESOLVED. Exact numeric comparisons; no floating tolerance.
